scopeDeviations.actual: Bypassed route() via direct call_model() for gpt-5-4 and gemini-pro architecture calls.
scopeDeviations.rationale: The operator-tuned router-config.yaml has architecture in auto_verify_task_types, meaning every route() call on this task type would trigger a redundant cross-provider verifier on each of the two routed calls (gpt-5-4-mini for gemini-pro; opus for gpt-5-4), duplicating the manual tri-provider review the session was running. The spec explicitly permits this fallback: 'If a force_model parameter isn't supported in the operator-tuned config, the orchestrator may directly invoke each provider via the underlying router primitive.' Both calls were recorded via record_call() so cost telemetry remained intact.

scopeDeviations.actual: Routed gpt-5-4 at reasoning_effort=high instead of the task_type_params default reasoning_effort=xhigh, with provider timeout bumped from 300s to 600s.
scopeDeviations.rationale: xhigh + 60KB prompt exceeded the 300s OpenAI timeout three times in a row (15 min wall, ~$0 in returned tokens). Retry at the model's default 'high' completed in 187s and produced a substantive 10.7K-token review. Future high-token architecture prompts (>50KB input) should adopt this pattern: either drop the task_type_params override for these prompts or bump the provider timeout.

deferredItems.item: Spec ambiguity between Step 2 ('the prompt should be identical across the three providers and self-contained — assume each reviewer has no prior context') and Step 3 ('the orchestrator writes its own assessment of the review prompt directly — the orchestrator already has the full context loaded').
deferredItems.deferred_to: Step 9 reorganization review (final session of this set, Session 11) — spec-revision item, not a session-4-internal fix.
deferredItems.rationale: These two clauses carry conflicting requirements. Step 3 explicitly cites 'the orchestrator already has the full context loaded' as the reason for self-contribution, which directly contradicts Step 2's 'no prior context' clause. The orchestrator-self-contribution pattern documented in feedback_orchestrator_self_contributes_to_review_panel was designed precisely to leverage the orchestrator's full context — re-doing Opus's assessment under strict prompt-only constraint would dismantle the pattern (functionally equivalent to routing Opus→Opus, which the feedback memory specifically advises against because it pays the API bill twice for the same judgment). Resolution requires a spec edit that picks one reading and spells it out unambiguously, OR a workflow-doc clarification that resolves the ambiguity globally. The substance of Session 4's tri-provider review (verdict, gap list, dispositions, no-pause conclusion) is sound regardless of which reading wins; only the methodology label changes.

followOnSpecsCalledOut.name: session-set-authoring-guide.md update (Step 9 reorganization scope)
followOnSpecsCalledOut.rationale: Resolve the Step 2 vs Step 3 ambiguity for tri-provider review sessions: either say 'the routed prompt is self-contained but the orchestrator's self-contribution may use the orchestrator's full context' (the position this session took), or 'all tri-provider review panel members operate on the same prompt-only context, including the orchestrator's self-contribution' (the strict-self-contained position). Pick one and update the spec template in session-set-authoring-guide.md so future tri-provider review sessions are unambiguous.

reason.specifics: Routed analysis (gemini-pro, $0.0038) recommended Claude Code Opus high for Session 5, matching the original spec ai-assignment recommendation. Session 5 (Packaging Approach Articulation And Tri-Provider Review) requires the orchestrator to (a) draft a complex multi-faceted technical proposal directly and (b) synthesize three independent architectural reviews of it. Same task profile as Session 4 — direct authoring + tri-provider synthesis — which Claude Opus performed effectively despite scope extensions and a 4-round verification arc. The cost and verification patterns from Session 4 reinforce the need for a top-tier model rather than a cheaper alternative.

notes: Session 4 produced the consolidated tri-provider value review with verdict 'yes-with-caveats' and 23 disposition'd gaps. All three reviewers (Opus, GPT-5.4, Gemini Pro) converged on proceed-with-packaging-but-tighten-the-external-story. The most consequential discovery during fix-now investigation: DabblerPdf is a port of OpenPDF and therefore dual-licensed LGPL-2.1-only OR MPL-2.0, NOT MIT. This is a compliance-critical detail that the original reviewers flagged only as 'undocumented dependency'; the fix-now investigation upgraded it to 'undocumented dependency WITH copyleft license that may deter enterprise adopters'. Disclosure landed in three docs: platform-overview.md (about-DabblerPdf paragraph + license aggregation note), Reports.Export/README.md, Reports.Core/README.md. The 4-round verification arc surfaced a real spec ambiguity (Step 2 'self-contained' vs Step 3 'orchestrator already has full context') that future tri-provider review specs need to resolve unambiguously. Documented as deferred for Step 9 reorganization review at session-set close.
